atlas-be.0124: Applications work at large firms; in the EU bubble, contacts made as a trainee count most.
atlas-be.0125: Duo for a JOB says referrals and word of mouth matter a lot, while EURES notes that many jobs are hidden.
atlas-be.0126: EURES covers the regional services and Actiris explains its services in 22 languages; for non-EU applicants the salary floors for a single permit apply to any offer.
atlas-be.0127: Brussels ads often ask for English plus French or Dutch; a study of 1,000 job offers found that command of all three opens the most doors.
atlas-be.0128: In that sample 915 offers were written in French, 58 in English and 18 in Dutch; of the 582 that named a language, French appeared in just over 80%, Dutch in 73% and English in 48%.
atlas-be.0129: BNP Paribas Fortis always holds at least two interviews and adds tests for some roles; Expatica says some jobs include psychometric, intelligence or aptitude tests, and the Brussels Times describes screening that is often AI-assisted, then a recruiter’s brief look at the CV.
atlas-be.0130: The interview starts with small talk and becomes fairly formal: dress smartly, arrive on time, shake hands, use the interviewer’s title, use “vous” until invited otherwise and bring a few questions; a short thank-you email afterwards is advised.
atlas-be.0131: In Brussels many companies accept applications in English or French, and the language of the ad sets the language of the application; the pages read give no typical time from application to offer.
atlas-be.0132: Probation periods were abolished on 1 January 2014, except in student and temporary-work contracts. Fixed-term, part-time, student and temporary contracts must be in writing; the contract states the gross salary, and employees pay about 13.07% in social security contributions.
atlas-be.0133: Collective agreements may add benefits such as a year-end bonus, so ask which joint committee covers the employer and compare offers on the yearly package, not the monthly figure alone.
atlas-be.0134: Notice for a resignation is proportional to seniority and can never exceed 13 weeks, for notices served since 28 October 2023.
atlas-be.0135: Graduate programmes are permanent full-time contracts at BNP Paribas Fortis and KBC; the pages read do not say how long you have to accept an offer.
atlas-be.0136: Each region sets its own salary floor for highly qualified single-permit workers in 2026: Wallonia €53,220 a year (€42,576 under 30), Brussels €3,703.44 a month and Flanders €48,912 a year (€39,129.60 under 30). The floor counts only fixed base salary.
atlas-be.0137: Some professional-card applications in Brussels have taken up to five months, so raise the permit at the offer stage; an employer that has filed one before is a safer bet than a small firm that has not.
atlas-be.0138: Programmes ask for the right to work: UCB’s Graduate Development Programme lists legal right to work in Belgium as a condition, so non-EU graduates should check that before applying. The Blue Book admits non-EU nationals to only a limited number of places.
atlas-be.0139: Public services: VDAB for Flanders (100,000 jobs on the day read), Actiris for Brussels and Le Forem for Wallonia, with EURES covering all of them and the German-speaking Community’s ADG.
atlas-be.0140: Graduate content: Student.be lists fairs, company events and first jobs for new graduates; Jobat.be and Références run Job Fair Brussels; Deloitte, BNP Paribas Fortis, KBC, Proximus and UCB post their programmes on their own careers pages.
atlas-be.0141: Public jobs and EU: EURES lists Selor for public-sector posts, and the Commission’s Blue Book site takes traineeship registrations.
atlas-be.0142: Other channels: EURES names company websites, job boards, recruitment and temporary agencies and LinkedIn, and some newspapers still publish vacancies at weekends.
atlas-be.0143: Writing in the wrong language: match the language of the ad, French in Wallonia and Brussels, Dutch in Flanders and Brussels, and have a native speaker check anything in a second language.
atlas-be.0144: Assuming English is enough: even in Brussels, French was named in over 80% of the offers that named a language, and Dutch in 73%.
atlas-be.0145: Putting age, nationality, marital status or gender on the CV, or attaching diplomas to it: EURES advises leaving the first four off, and diplomas go to the interview.
atlas-be.0146: Sending a cover letter with another company’s name left in it, or one that repeats the CV instead of showing motivation.
atlas-be.0147: Treating the EU competition as an entry route: 174,727 people applied for 1,490 places in 2026, so a Blue Book traineeship or contract-agent post is the realistic first door, and its registration window is under four weeks.
atlas-be.0148: KBC’s commercial track asks for very good spoken and written Dutch; in the Actiris sample, 78.43% of offers in real estate, insurance, finance and law named a language requirement. No certificate is named: the interview is the test.
atlas-be.0149: In the Actiris sample 63.64% of administration and accounting offers named a language, and several Big Four advisory teams work in English.
atlas-be.0150: Business management and services offers named a language in 74.51% of the Actiris sample; Big Four advisory teams often work in English, and a trilingual profile (French, Dutch, English) opens the most doors.
atlas-be.0151: UCB’s Graduate Development Programme lists fluent English as mandatory and does not mention French or Dutch; the evidence is a short application questionnaire, not a certificate.
atlas-be.0152: The Blue Book asks EU nationals for C1 or C2 in English, French or German and B2 in a second EU language; non-EU applicants need C1 in one of the three.
atlas-be.0153: In the Actiris sample 80% of IT offers named a language; Proximus describes its workplace as multilingual and lists no required language for its programme.
atlas-be.0154: In 2025, 90.2% of Belgians aged 20 to 34 with a tertiary degree were in work, and 88.5% of those who left education within the last five years, against unemployment of 17.4% among all 15-to-24-year-olds.
atlas-be.0155: The job vacancy rate fell from 4.1% in the last quarter of 2024 to 3.5% in the last quarter of 2025, with 5.4% in professional, scientific and technical activities and 2.9% in finance and insurance, so the entry market is cooling.
atlas-be.0156: No source read gives a return-offer or conversion rate for Belgian internships or graduate programmes, nor a time to first job for internationals.
atlas-be.0158: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens need no visa, work permit or quota.
atlas-be.0159: Within three months, register at your commune (Annexe 19). Since 1 September 2025 the file must be complete on day one, with the employer’s form or your contract, or for students the enrolment, health cover and proof of means; an incomplete file is refused at once.
atlas-be.0160: A local police officer checks you live at the address; then you receive the EU card, valid five years, for €25 to €35.
atlas-be.0162: Pay the federal fee to the immigration office, apply for the D visa at the embassy, then register at your commune within eight working days of arriving; after the police address check you receive an A card for the academic year.
atlas-be.0163: Prove funds through a blocked account at the university, a sponsor’s guarantee (Annexe 32) or a scholarship. You may work 20 hours a week in term and without limit in holidays.
atlas-be.0164: A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country in an EU mobility programme needs no Belgian visa: the university notifies the immigration office, and you can stay up to 360 days.
atlas-be.0171: An internship that is part of a recognised degree programme, Belgian or from the EEA, needs no work authorisation and no single permit.
atlas-be.0173: For people aged 18 to 30: the company applies for a single permit for trainees with a training plan approved by the region; at most 12 months, and the trainee must be paid.
atlas-be.0175: Job-search year after a Belgian degree
atlas-be.0176: After a bachelor’s, master’s or doctorate in Belgium, or at the end of a research stay: 12 months, not renewable, in which you may take any job full time.
atlas-be.0177: A qualified job then converts it inside Belgium, at the lower under-30 salary in Flanders and Wallonia.
atlas-be.0179: Apply at your commune at least 15 days before your student card expires: later, the application is inadmissible and you are ordered to leave.
atlas-be.0180: Single permit for highly qualified work
atlas-be.0181: Only the Belgian employer can apply, through Working in Belgium. A three-year degree and a salary above the region’s threshold exempt the job from the labour-market test.
atlas-be.0189: No one can apply for a single permit for you for a fee: offers to do so are scams.
atlas-be.0191: A contract of at least six months and a three-year degree, or three (IT) to five years of experience in the last seven; the H card lasts up to three years, and a spouse joins at once with the right to work.
